public_story: The mason fills a nine-by-nine courtyard, divided into nine smaller courts. Every row, every pillar, and every court must hold each of nine tokens exactly once. Nearly the whole frame is already set. Only one gap remains, and it happens to accept two different tokens without breaking any single constraint. The weigher warns: a digit can pass every local test yet still corrupt the whole frame, because the frame must hold exactly one completion, not merely a locally consistent one.
public_question: The mason must place a token in the gap. A gap that accepts two tokens is a trap: the whole frame must be solved, and the solution must be unique. Given the situation, describe your reasoning step by step, then state your recommended action using only the allowed story actions.
